Not every BOJ dataset is best represented as a time-series API call. The
package also supports the official bulk-file catalogue and dated Tankan
comprehensive-data release pages. The workflow is intentionally two-stage:
discover an official URL, then download and parse the exact file. The parser
keeps source hashes and applies archive, row, sheet, and cell bounds.

The default examples below are offline. The local CSV and workbook created in
this article contain synthetic values solely to exercise the parsers; they are
not BOJ releases.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", width = 78)
library(readboj)

fixture_file <- function(name) {
  path <- system.file("extdata", name, package = "readboj")
  if (!nzchar(path)) {
    candidates <- c(file.path("inst", "extdata", name),
      file.path("..", "inst", "extdata", name))
    path <- candidates[file.exists(candidates)][1L]
  }
  if (!nzchar(path) || !file.exists(path)) stop("Fixture is unavailable: ", name)
  normalizePath(path, mustWork = TRUE)
}
```

## Read a bulk CSV with markers intact

`read_boj_bulk()` accepts a local CSV or the `boj_file` path returned by
`download_boj_bulk()`. A headerless long file is interpreted as
`series_code`, `frequency`, `period`, and `value`. Values stay character in
the source column, with convenient numeric/status companions:

```{r bulk-csv}
bulk_path <- tempfile("readboj-bulk-", fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c(
  "SYNTHM01,MONTHLY,202601,101.5",
  "SYNTHM01,MONTHLY,202602,NA",
  "SYNTHM01,MONTHLY,202603,ND"
), bulk_path, useBytes = TRUE)

bulk_data <- read_boj_bulk(bulk_path, max_rows = 10L)
bulk_data[, c(
  "series_code", "frequency", "period", "value", "value_numeric",
  "value_status"
)]
invisible(unlink(bulk_path))
```

The original `value` markers (`"NA"` and `"ND"`) are not discarded. Their
`value_numeric` values are `NA`, and `value_status` identifies the marker.
For a ZIP archive, the same function validates entry paths and aggregate
uncompressed sizes before extracting CSV members. If one CSV is present it
returns a data frame; multiple CSVs are returned as a named `boj_bulk` list.

## Read a bounded workbook as text

Official workbooks often contain identifiers, labels, suppression markers,
and presentation sheets rather than a tidy time-series table. `read_boj_workbook()`
therefore reads selected sheets as text and does not silently coerce an
identifier or marker to a number. The following creates a tiny synthetic
workbook when the optional `writexl` package is available:

```{r workbook}
if (requireNamespace("writexl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  workbook_path <- tempfile("readboj-workbook-", fileext = ".xlsx")
  writexl::write_xlsx(list(catalogue = data.frame(
    series_code = c("SYNTHM01", "SYNTHM02"),
    unit = c("Index", "Percent"),
    marker = c("ND", "NA"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )), workbook_path)

  workbook <- read_boj_workbook(
    workbook_path,
    sheets = "catalogue",
    max_rows_per_sheet = 10L,
    max_columns = 10L,
    max_cells = 100L
  )
  workbook$catalogue
  boj_provenance(workbook)[c("raw_sha256", "parser", "sheets", "cells")]
  invisible(unlink(workbook_path))
}
```

The result is a named list of data frames. Use the `sheets`, `max_rows_per_sheet`,
`max_columns`, and `max_cells` arguments to make a report's resource budget
explicit. This reader is structural: it does not infer a time-series schema
or join survey breaks for you.

## Discover official bulk and Tankan files

The catalogue and Tankan functions use live official HTML pages, so they are
shown only in an explicitly opt-in block. They can be pointed at an explicit
cache directory and replayed later with `offline = TRUE`:

```{r live-file-discovery}
live <- identical(Sys.getenv("READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES"), "true")
if (live) {
  cache <- file.path(tempdir(), "readboj-file-cache")

  bulk_catalogue <- list_boj_bulk_files(
    language = "en", cache_dir = cache,
    timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0, max_bytes = 2 * 1024^2,
    deadline = Sys.time() + 30
  )
  archives <- bulk_catalogue[bulk_catalogue$role == "data_archive", , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(archives)) {
    bulk_file <- download_boj_bulk(
      archives$id[[1L]], language = "en", cache_dir = cache,
      timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0, max_bytes = 20 * 1024^2,
      deadline = Sys.time() + 45
    )
    bulk_result <- read_boj_bulk(
      bulk_file, max_uncompressed_bytes = 50 * 1024^2,
      max_rows = 100000L
    )
    boj_provenance(bulk_file)
  }

  releases <- list_boj_tankan_releases(
    language = "en", cache_dir = cache, max_pages = 6L,
    timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0, max_bytes = 2 * 1024^2,
    deadline = Sys.time() + 60
  )
  if (nrow(releases)) {
    assets <- list_boj_tankan_assets(
      releases$url[[1L]], cache_dir = cache,
      timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0, max_bytes = 2 * 1024^2,
      deadline = Sys.time() + 30
    )
    xlsx <- assets$url[grepl("\\.xlsx?$", assets$url, ignore.case = TRUE)]
    if (length(xlsx)) {
      tankan_file <- download_boj_tankan_asset(
        xlsx[[1L]], cache_dir = cache,
        timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0,
        max_bytes = 20 * 1024^2, deadline = Sys.time() + 45
      )
      boj_provenance(tankan_file)
    }
  }
} else {
  message("Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to run this live example.")
}
```

`list_boj_bulk_files()` is selected current catalogue coverage, not a promise
that every API database has a bulk file. `list_boj_tankan_releases()` tracks
dated comprehensive-data pages from the official archive, while
`list_boj_tankan_assets()` admits only XLS/XLSX and ZIP links from a release
page. PDF notices and unrelated links are not treated as data assets.

No credentials are required or accepted. Network requests are HTTPS-only and
restricted to official BOJ hosts. Documented request, bound, and schema
failures use typed conditions, and an unsuccessful response is not cached as
a successful data object. Dependency errors from a malformed third-party file
may retain their original class and should be reported with the file identity.
